parts.name: frame steel

physics.Basic_description: The main body of the wrench head and shaft, appearing as a matte grey metallic structure with a rectangular profile and cutouts for the jaw mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural frame that holds the fixed jaw and guides the movable jaw and adjustment nut.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can grasp the neck or the head frame firmly to apply torque, though the handle is preferred for leverage.
physics.reason: Wrench heads are typically forged or cast from solid steel to withstand high torsional forces without deforming.

parts.description: The main body of the wrench head and shaft, appearing as a matte grey metallic structure with a rectangular profile and cutouts for the jaw mechanism.
parts.function: Provides the structural frame that holds the fixed jaw and guides the movable jaw and adjustment nut.

parts.name: flat handle

physics.Basic_description: A long, slender, cylindrical grey metal rod extending from the head, featuring a looped end for hanging.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the lever arm for the user to apply rotational force to the fastener.
physics.Grasped_description: The primary grasp point for a robot; a parallel jaw gripper should clamp around the mid-section of the handle to maximize leverage.
physics.reason: Handles of hand tools are solid metal rods or bars to prevent bending under load.

parts.description: A long, slender, cylindrical grey metal rod extending from the head, featuring a looped end for hanging.
parts.function: Acts as the lever arm for the user to apply rotational force to the fastener.

parts.name: jaw steel

physics.Basic_description: A blocky grey metal component situated within the head frame, designed to slide linearly.
physics.Functional_description: Moves in and out to adjust the width of the wrench opening to fit different nut sizes.
physics.Grasped_description: Not intended for grasping during normal operation; manipulating this part directly would require fine motor skills to adjust the jaw width.
physics.reason: The movable jaw is a solid block of hardened steel to resist crushing forces against the fastener.

parts.name: nut knurled

physics.Basic_description: A small, knurled cylindrical wheel located on the side of the wrench head, appearing slightly distinct in texture.
physics.Functional_description: Rotated by the thumb to drive the worm gear that translates the movable jaw.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped by a fine-tip gripper or manipulated by a finger-like probe to rotate and adjust the jaw opening.
physics.reason: The adjustment nut is a small, dense metal component, effectively solid for mass estimation purposes.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
